s:
A company has many services running in its on-premises data center. The data center is connected to AWS using AWS Direct Connect (DX)and an IPsec VPN. The service data is sensitive and connectivity

cannot traverse the interne. The company wants to expand to a new market segment and begin offering Is services to other companies that are using AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Create a VPC Endpoint Service that accepts TCP traffic, host it behind a Network Load Balancer, and make the service available over DX.
Create a VPC Endpoint Service that accepts HTTP or HTTPS traffic, host it behind an Application Load Balancer, and make the service available over DX.
Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. and ensure that network access control and security group rules allow the relevant inbound and outbound traffic.
Attach a NAT gateway to the VPC. and ensue that network access control and security group rules allow the relevant inbound and outbound traffic.
e: To offer services to other companies using AWS without traversing the internet, creating a VPC Endpoint Service hosted behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and making it available over AWS Direct Connect (DX) is the most suitable solution. This approach ensures that the service traffic remains within the AWS network, adhering to the requirement that connectivity must not traverse the internet. An ALB is capable of handlingHTTP/HTTPS traffic, making it appropriate for web-based services. Utilizing DX for connectivity between the on-premises data center and AWS further secures and optimizes the network path. AWS Direct Connect Documentation: Explains how to set up DX for private connectivity between AWS and an on-premises network. Amazon VPC Endpoint Services (AWS PrivateLink) Documentation: Provides details on creating and configuring endpoint services for private, secure access to services hosted in AWS. AWS Application Load Balancer Documentation: Offers guidance on configuring ALBs to distribute HTTP/HTTPS traffic efficiently.

w.y: The deciding words are 'offer services to other companies on AWS' and 'cannot traverse the internet'. A VPC endpoint service (PrivateLink) must be backed by a Network Load Balancer (or Gateway Load Balancer); the NLB can target on-premises IPs reached over Direct Connect.

o.A: Correct: PrivateLink endpoint services use an NLB, which can front on-premises services over Direct Connect.
o.B: An ALB cannot be the load balancer for a VPC endpoint service.
o.C: An internet gateway exposes the service over the internet.
o.D: A NAT gateway is for outbound traffic and exposes nothing to other companies privately.
